name: Regulatory costs

subjectOf.text: If coordinated international regulation forces hedge funds out, the funds can absorb the costs of relocating offshore while the market segments and jurisdictions they leave will inevitably suffer.
subjectOf.abstract: Hedge funds may be able to afford to relocate off- shore with all its detrimental repercussions, i.e. costs, client losses etc. but certain market segments and jurisdictions will inevitably suffer when all its hedge funds are forced out.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Indirect Regulation of Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3405660
scope_conditions: coordinated international cooperation is actually implemented

subjectOf.text: Indirect regulation minimizes regulatory expense by relying on the private sector risk practices of counterparties and creditors, producing an equilibrium between regulatory cost and regulatory attainment.
subjectOf.abstract: Relying on private sector practices by counterparties and creditors minimizes regulatory expenses significantly. Indirect regulation enables a state of equilibrium between costs and attainments of regulatory initiatives.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Indirect Regulation of Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3405660
scope_conditions: counterparties and creditors actually maintain disciplined private sector practices

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'regulatory-costs'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
